Nigel Farage: British politician and broadcaster (born 1964)
A protégé of Tage Erlander, this Swedish prime minister led the Social Democrats from 1969 until he was assassinated in 1986 — who was he?
Olof Palme: Prime Minister of Sweden (1969–76; 1982–86)
Serving as Speaker pro tempore for 22 days after Kevin McCarthy's removal, this North Carolina Republican chaired the House Financial Services Committee from 2023 to 2025 — who is he?
Serving as Vietnam's eighth prime minister from 2021 to 2026, this former lieutenant general once led the Communist Party's organizing commission — who is he?

Phạm Minh Chính: Prime Minister of Vietnam from 2021 to 2026. Phạm Minh Chính (Vietnamese: [faːm˧˨ʔ mïŋ˧˧ t͡ɕïŋ˧˦]; born 10 December 1958) is a Vietnamese politician and former public security lieutenant general.
Built on power concentrated among 'siloviks' from Russia's security services, this system of governance has been likened to Stalinism as a 21st-century watchword — what is it called?
Putinism: Political system in Russia under Vladimir Putin.

Turkish politician who rose from Istanbul mayor to prime minister (2003–2014) and has been president since 2014, co-founding the AKP. His rule has drawn criticism for democratic backsliding. Who is he?
Recep Tayyip Erdoğan: President of Turkey since 2014. Recep Tayyip Erdoğan (born 26 February 1954) is a Turkish politician and statesman who has been the president of Turkey since 2014.
The first person to walk to both the North and South Poles, this explorer later led his son on a 600-mile renewable-energy-only trek to the South Pole in 2017 — who is he?
A key figure in Japan's Meiji Restoration, this samurai later led a doomed 1877 uprising against the very government he helped create, dying in the fighting — who was he?
Saigō Takamori: Japanese samurai and politician (1828–1877)
A billionaire businessman who studied economics at Harvard, this politician served two separate terms as president of Chile between 2010 and 2022 — who was he?
Emulating the medieval chevauchée, this scorched-earth 1864 Civil War campaign cut from Atlanta to the captured port of Savannah. What was it called?
Sherman's March to the Sea: 1864 military campaign of the American Civil War.

Considered erotic poetry unlike other biblical books, this text narrates a passionate dialogue between a woman and her lover, warning the 'daughters of Jerusalem' not to awaken love too soon — what is it?
Song of Songs: Book of the Hebrew Bible and the Christian Old Testament.
Nicknamed the 'Tiger King' for his ferocity, this 29th monarch of the Ayutthaya Kingdom is credited with devising the fundamental techniques of Muay Thai — who is he?
Known by a name meaning 'behind the pool' after the palace where he resided, this monarch ruled the Ayutthaya Kingdom from 1709 to 1733 as the third ruler of the Ban Phlu Luang dynasty — who is he?
Thai Sa: King of Ayutthaya. The name "Thai Sa" (lit. "behind the pool") refers to the Banyongrattanat Palace, which was located by a pool where he often resided.

Japan's first socialist premier in nearly half a century, this 1990s prime minister is best remembered for an official statement apologizing for his country's past colonial wars on the 50th anniversary of WWII's end. Who was he?
Tomiichi Murayama: Prime Minister of Japan from 1994 to 1996.
This four-star general led Ukraine's Armed Forces as Commander-in-Chief from 2021 until February 2024, then traded the battlefield for the role of Ambassador to the United Kingdom — who is he?
Valerii Zaluzhnyi: Ukrainian general and diplomat (born 1973)

Highly regarded as a military strategist, this Vietnamese general led communist forces to victory across the decades-long Indochina wars, while also serving as minister of defense and deputy prime minister. Who is he?
Võ Nguyên Giáp: Vietnamese general and communist politician (1911–2013)

A paratrooper with Easy Company's 101st Airborne in World War II, this veteran co-wrote a memoir with fellow soldier 'Babe' Heffron and was portrayed by Frank John Hughes in a famed HBO miniseries — who is he?
Serving as head of state under Lenin's new government until his death in 1919, this Bolshevik organizer of the October Revolution also chaired the party's Secretariat — who was he?
Founder of the Pakistan People's Party, this barrister-statesman served as both president and prime minister of Pakistan before his 1977 overthrow and 1979 execution — who was he?
Zulfikar Ali Bhutto: 4th President and 9th Prime Minister of Pakistan (1928–1979)
Who among these was born first?
Jabir ibn Hayyan (born 721) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
Patrick Geddes (born 1854) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four has been around longest?

Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four. Fortran (formerly FORTRAN) is a third-generation, compiled, imperative programming language designed for numeric computation and scientific computing.
Which of these four is the oldest?
Pascal (programming language) (founded 1970) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these is an astronomer?
Dorothea Klumpke is an astronomer. Dorothea Klumpke Roberts (August 9, 1861 in San Francisco – October 5, 1942 in San Francisco) was an American astronomer.
Which one below is best known as a mathematician?
Georg Cantor is a mathematician. Cantor's method of proof of this theorem implies the existence of an infinity of infinities.
What is the atomic number of Thorium?
Thorium is a chemical element; it has symbol Th and atomic number 90.
What is the atomic number of Osmium?
Osmium (from Ancient Greek ὀσμή (osmḗ) 'smell') is a chemical element; it has symbol Os and atomic number 76.
In what year was Scott Cawthon born?
Scott Cawthon: Cawthon began his career developing family-friendly Christian video games to minimal success.
In what year was Brian Cox born?
Brian Cox (physicist): Brian Edward Cox (born 3 March 1968) is an English physicist and musician.
In what year was Nikola Tesla born?
Nikola Tesla (10 July 1856 – 7 January 1943) was a Serbian-American engineer, futurist, and inventor.
In what year did Homi J. Bhabha die?
Homi J. Bhabha: Bhabha was awarded the Adams Prize (1942) and Padma Bhushan (1954), and nominated for the Nobel Prize for Physics in 1951 and 1953–1956.
In what year did Enrico Fermi die?
Enrico Fermi: With his colleagues, Fermi filed several patents related to the use of nuclear power, all of which were taken over by the US government.
In what year was Beryllium discovered?
Beryllium is a chemical element; it has symbol Be and atomic number 4.
Eurocopter Tiger: Airbus Helicopters. The Eurocopter EC665 Tiger, is a four-blade, twin-engine attack helicopter which first entered service in 2003.
In which country is Harrier jump jet?
Harrier jump jet: United Kingdom. The Harrier emerged as the only truly successful V/STOL design of the many attempted during that era.
Fufu: Ghana. Fufu (or fufuo, foofoo, foufou foo-foo) is a pounded meal found in West African cuisine.
Who is credited with discovering Tennessine?
Tennessine: Yuri Oganessian. Tennessine is a synthetic element; it has symbol Ts and atomic number 117.
Who is credited with discovering Ammonia?
Ammonia: Joseph Priestley. Ammonia is an inorganic chemical compound of nitrogen and hydrogen with the formula NH3.
Who is credited with discovering Selenium?
Selenium: Jöns Jacob Berzelius. Selenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Se and atomic number 34.
A King's College Cambridge graduate who earned a Princeton doctorate in 1938, he later joined Britain's wartime codebreaking effort and pioneered theoretical computing — who was he?
Alan Turing (23 June 1912 - 7 June 1954) was an English mathematician, computer scientist, logician, cryptanalyst, philosopher and theoretical biologist.
Despite overseeing Soviet thermonuclear weapons development, this physicist won the 1975 Nobel Peace Prize for his activism on human rights and individual freedom — who is he?
Andrei Sakharov (21 May 1921 - 14 December 1989) was a Soviet physicist and a Nobel Peace Prize laureate, which he was awarded in 1975 for emphasizing human rights around the world.

Which plant family of about 181 genera and 2,600 species, nearly all found in the tropics, includes climbers, shrubs, and tree-like forms with large fan- or feather-shaped fronds atop mostly unbranched stems?
Arecaceae are a family of perennial, flowering plants in the monocot order Arecales.
Native to the Mekong and Chao Phraya river basins, this freshwater catfish is marketed in the US as "swai" and in the UK as "river cobbler" — which fish?

Basa (fish) (Pangasius bocourti), as it is commonly referred to, is a species of primarily freshwater-dwelling catfish in the shark-catfish family, Pangasiidae, native to the Mekong and Chao Phraya river basins of Mainland Southeast Asia.
Despite its name, this sub-Saharan snake is actually grey to dark brown — the second-longest venomous snake in the world after the king cobra, commonly reaching 3 meters — name this species?
Black mamba (Dendroaspis polylepis) is a species of highly venomous snake belonging to the family Elapidae.
With a mass roughly 13 to 80 times Jupiter's, these substellar objects glow faintly from deuterium fusion rather than true hydrogen burning — what's the term for them?
Brown dwarf are substellar objects that have more mass than the biggest gas giant planets, but less than the least massive main-sequence stars.
Its name comes from the Latin for "coal," and one of its isotopes decays with a 5,700-year half-life that lets scientists date ancient remains — which element is it?
Carbon (from Latin carbo 'coal') is a chemical element; it has symbol C and atomic number 6.
Along with the bonobo, which great ape of equatorial Africa's forests and savannas is humans' closest living relative, according to DNA and fossil evidence?
Chimpanzee (Pan troglodytes), also simply known as the chimp, is a medium-sized great ape species found in the forests and savannas of equatorial Africa.
This digestive condition refers to swelling or inflammation of the large intestine, and can be acute and short-lived or a long-term, chronic issue — what is it called?
Colitis is swelling or inflammation of the large intestine (colon). It broadly fits into the category of digestive diseases.
These echinoderms come in stalked "sea lily" and free-swimming "feather star" forms, with mouths on their upper surface ringed by feeding arms — what class of marine animal is it?
Crinoid are marine invertebrates that make up the class Crinoidea.

Generally moving particles, energy, or other quantities from regions of higher concentration to lower, this stochastic physical process is driven by a gradient in Gibbs free energy and can occasionally even run 'uphill' via spinodal decomposition — name this process?
Diffusion is the net movement of anything (for example, atoms, ions, molecules, energy) generally from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.
Born in North Carolina in 1983, this former NSA contractor leaked classified files exposing global surveillance programs after working for the CIA, Dell, and a defense contractor — name him?

Edward Snowden (born June 21, 1983) is a former United States National Security Agency (NSA) intelligence contractor who leaked classified documents revealing the existence of global surveillance programs.
This flowering plant in the family Erythroxylaceae is one of just two species cultivated for their alkaloid-rich leaves — what is its scientific name?
Erythroxylum coca is a species of flowering plant in the family Erythroxylaceae.
Which evergreen conifer genus has needle-like leaves attached singly to the branch by a circular base, and cones that stand upright like a cedar's rather than hanging down? What is it?
Fir are evergreen coniferous trees belonging to the genus Abies in the family Pinaceae.
Named for a long-nosed, insect-eating African animal, this retired supersonic fighter-bomber pioneered variable-sweep wings and automated terrain-following radar in the 1960s — which aircraft?
General Dynamics F-111 Aardvark is a retired, supersonic, medium-range fighter-bomber.
Also called the woodchuck, this North American rodent is exceptional among its kin: while most marmots live in rocky mountains, this lowland burrower roams the Eastern U.S. into Alaska — what is it?
Groundhog (Marmota monax), also known as the woodchuck, is a rodent of the family Sciuridae, belonging to the group of large ground squirrels known as marmots.
A member of the human Herpesviridae family, this contagious pathogen comes in two types, with about 67% of people under 50 carrying the first as of 2016. What is it?
Herpes simplex virus (HSV-1 and HSV-2) are two members of the human Herpesviridae family, a set of viruses that produce viral infections in the majority of humans.
Defined by Whipple's triad, this condition occurs when blood sugar falls below about 70 mg/dL, causing symptoms like headache, shakiness, confusion, and a fast heart rate — what's it called?

Hypoglycemia (American English), also spelled hypoglycaemia or hypoglycmia (British English), sometimes called low blood sugar, is a fall in blood sugar to levels below normal, typically below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L).
Widely planted outside its native South America for its striking purple flowers, this tree is considered Vulnerable in the wild according to the IUCN — which species?
Jacaranda mimosifolia is a sub-tropical tree native to south-central South America that has been widely planted elsewhere because of its attractive and long-lasting violet-colored flowers.
Holding doctorates in both anthropology and medicine, this SS physician earned the grim nickname 'Angel of Death' for his experiments and selections at Auschwitz — who was he?

Josef Mengele (16 March 1911 - 7 February 1979), often dubbed the "Angel of Death", was a German military officer and physician during World War II at the Soviet front and then at Auschwitz during the Holocaust.
Home to aromatic herbs like mint, oregano, and lavender as well as the seed crop chia, this family of mostly herbaceous flowering plants is commonly known as the mints or deadnettles — which family?

Lamiaceae is a family of flowering plants commonly known as mints, deadnettles, or sages. The mint family as a whole has a cosmopolitan distribution comprising about 236 genera and around 6,900 to 7,200 species.
This ACE inhibitor can take up to four weeks for full effect and is also used to prevent kidney problems in people with diabetes — which medication?
Lisinopril is a medication belonging to the drug class of angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors and is used to treat hypertension (high blood pressure), heart failure, and heart attacks.
Recognizable by the male's iridescent green head, this widespread dabbling duck species has been introduced to countries from New Zealand to South Africa far beyond its native range — what is it?
Mallard (Anas platyrhynchos) is a dabbling duck that breeds throughout the temperate and subtropical Americas, Eurasia, and North Africa.
Crushed leaves of this mint-family herb smell like spearmint, yet it has caused deaths when used as a traditional abortifacient — which species, also known as pennyroyal?

Mentha pulegium (European) pennyroyal, or pennyrile, also called mosquito plant and pudding grass, is a species of flowering plant in the mint family, Lamiaceae, native to Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East.
A small terrestrial carnivore of the family Herpestidae that feasts mainly on insects, reptiles, and birds — and turns up as an introduced pest in Hawaii — what creature is it?
Mongoose is a small terrestrial carnivorous mammal belonging to the family Herpestidae.
A naval aviator who flew the F9F Panther in Korea before commanding Apollo 11, this Ohio-born engineer earned a place in history in 1969 — who is he?
Neil Armstrong (August 5, 1930 - August 25, 2012) was an American astronaut and aeronautical engineer who, as the commander of the 1969 Apollo 11 mission, became the first person to walk on the Moon.
Named after a German physicist, this SI unit of electrical resistance is represented by the uppercase Greek letter omega — name the unit?
Ohm (symbol:, the uppercase Greek letter omega) is the unit of electrical resistance in the International System of Units (SI).
Found in organs such as the brain and lungs, inside flatworms, and within leaf cross-sections, this word names an organism's bulk functional tissue — what is it?
Parenchyma is the bulk of functional substance in an animal organ such as the brain or lungs, or a structure such as a tumour.
Written by the Hong sisters, this South Korean series about young mages dealing with heaven and earth aired on tvN in two parts during 2022 and 2023. What show is it?
Pharynx (pl.: pharynges) is the part of the throat behind the mouth and nasal cavity, and above the esophagus and trachea (the tubes going down to the stomach and the lungs respectively).
Cough, chest pain, fever, and trouble breathing point to this infection of the lungs' alveoli, often classified by where it was caught — community or hospital — what is it?
Pneumonia is an inflammatory condition of the lung primarily affecting the small air sacs known as alveoli.
This rose-family genus of roughly 340 species includes almonds, apricots, and cherries, whose pit encloses a kernel that's edible in some species and poisonous in others — which genus?

Prunus is a genus of flowering trees and shrubs from the family Rosaceae, with about 340 accepted species (as of March 2024) that include peaches and nectarines, apricots, plums, cherries and almonds.
Belonging to the genus Ribes and native to western Europe, which berry carries the scientific name Ribes rubrum and has spread into the wild in many regions?
Redcurrant (Ribes rubrum) is a member of the genus Ribes in the family Grossulariaceae.
Mostly used in wear-resistant electrical contacts and thick-film resistors, which rare, chemically unreactive platinum-group metal has atomic number 44?
Ruthenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ru and atomic number 44.

This potentially life-threatening condition occurs when the body's dysregulated response to infection damages its own tissues and organs, often causing fever, rapid heartbeat, and confusion — what is it called?
Sepsis is a potentially life-threatening condition that arises when the body's dysregulated response to infection causes injury to its own tissues and organs.
Found throughout the nightshade family — including in potato leaves, fruit, and tubers — this saponin-family toxin doubles as the plant's own natural pesticide. What compound is it?
Solanine is a glycoalkaloid poison found in species of the nightshade family within the genus Solanum, such as the potato (Solanum tuberosum).
A Jamaican-British Marxist sociologist who co-founded New Left Review, this thinker became a founding figure of the Birmingham School of Cultural Studies — who was he?
Stuart Hall (cultural theorist) (3 February 1932 - 10 February 2014) was a Jamaican-British Marxist sociologist, cultural theorist, and political activist.
This American actress won an Oscar, three BAFTAs, two Tonys, and two Emmys, one of only 24 performers ever to complete acting's Triple Crown. Who is she?
Terry Gou (pinyin: Gu Timng; Peh-e-j: Koeh Ti-bng; born 18 October 1950) is a Taiwanese billionaire businessman and politician.
Caused by superantigens from staph or strep bacteria, this condition brings fever, a sunburn-like rash, and peeling skin, and has been tied to absorbent tampon use — which condition?
Toxic shock syndrome (TSS) is a condition caused by bacterial toxins.
This member of the herpesvirus family causes chickenpox in children and, upon reactivation later in life, shingles in adults — what is it called?
Varicella zoster virus (VZV), also known as human herpesvirus 3 (HHV-3, HHV3), is one of nine known herpes viruses that can infect humans.
Short-legged, muscular, and stubby-tailed, this Australian marsupial can reach about a metre long and tip the scales between 20 and 35 kilograms — what is it?
Wombat are short-legged, muscular quadrupedal marsupials of the family Vombatidae that are native to Australia.
Accidentally discovered in 1967 by German chemist Karl Clauss at Hoechst AG, which calorie-free artificial sweetener is sold under the brand names Sunett and Sweet One?

Designed to replace the Lockheed C-130 Hercules and sized between it and the Boeing C-17, this four-engine European turboprop military transporter first flew from Seville in December 2009 despite nearly being cancelled over cost overruns. What's the aircraft?
Airbus A400M Atlas: Multi-national four-engine turboprop military transport aircraft.
This mushroom genus contains the notorious 'death cap,' responsible for roughly 90% of all fatal mushroom poisonings worldwide — which genus?
Amanita: Genus of mushrooms. The genus is responsible for 95% of fatalities resulting from mushroom poisoning, with the death cap accounting for 90% of fatalities every year.

This psychological term describes reduced motivation or ability to experience pleasure, recognized in the DSM-5 as a component of depressive, substance-related, psychotic, and personality disorders. What is it called?
Nicknamed the 'Primeval Bird' in German, this magpie-sized, feathered dinosaur from 150-million-year-old Jurassic Germany was long hailed as the earliest known bird — what is it?
Archaeopteryx: Extinct genus of bird-like dinosaurs.
Sold as Lipitor, this first-line statin lowers cholesterol to fend off cardiovascular disease, with mild muscle aches among its better-known side effects — what's the drug?
A blood-feeding parasite of the genus Cimex that usually bites at night, this insect leaves itchy welts but, reassuringly, isn't known to spread any infectious disease — what is it?
Bed bug: Type of insect that feeds on human blood.
This class of aquatic molluscs — including clams, oysters, mussels, and scallops — has no head and encloses its soft body in a hinged pair of shells called valves — which class?
Bivalvia: Class of molluscs. The shell of a bivalve is composed of calcium carbonate, and consists of two, usually similar, parts called valves.

When a gas of bosons is cooled to within a hair of absolute zero, this state of matter, first predicted in 1924-25, sees a large fraction of particles pile into a single quantum state — what is it called?
Bose–Einstein condensate: State of matter. In 1995, the Bose–Einstein condensate was created by Eric Cornell and Carl Wieman of the University of Colorado Boulder using rubidium atoms.
Named after the Greek word for butter via butyric acid, this colorless, highly flammable gas exists as two isomers and vaporizes quickly at room temperature — what alkane is it?
Native to Africa, the Middle East, and arid parts of Asia, this nocturnal, secretive wild cat is built for the chase with long legs and dramatically long tufted ears — which animal?
Also called bachelor's button, this European annual once grew as a common weed among grain fields but is now endangered there due to herbicides — what flower is it?
Centaurea cyanus: Species of flowering plant.

Nicknamed for its spider-like look and also called airplane plant or hen and chicks, this houseplant is native to tropical Africa but can suffer 'burnt tips' from fluoride in tap water — which species?
Chlorophytum comosum: Species of flowering plant. It is native to tropical and Southern Africa but has become naturalized in other parts of the world, including Western Australia and Bangladesh.
Native to the Americas from Mexico to South America, this diurnal member of the Procyonidae family goes by the name 'quash' in Belize — what is it?

Known to NATO by the reporting name 'Mop' and to Canadian forces as the Canso, this WWII flying boat served every branch of the U.S. military and remained in some air forces into the 1980s — which aircraft?
Consolidated PBY Catalina: American 1930s flying boat.
This species includes honeydew, cantaloupe, and Casaba varieties, and traveled along ancient caravan routes long before its exact origin in the Levant or Egypt was ever confirmed — what fruit is it?
Cucumis melo: Species of plant. Cucumis melo, also known as melon or true melon, is a species of Cucumis that has been developed into many cultivated varieties.
Striking 48 to 72 hours after a heavy drinker's last drink, this potentially fatal condition brings hallucinations, seizures nicknamed 'rum fits,' and dangerously high body temperature — what is it?
Delirium tremens: Rapid onset of confusion caused by alcohol withdrawal.
Bred in Córdoba in the early 1900s to hunt wild boar and puma, this large mastiff-type breed's ancestry includes an extinct local fighting dog and a Bull Terrier — which breed is it?
Dogo Argentino: Argentine breed of dog. It was bred in the early twentieth century in Córdoba in central Argentina, primarily for hunting large game such as peccaries, wild boar, and pumas.
After stints at the CIA, Dell, and Booz Allen Hamilton, this NSA contractor flew to Hong Kong in 2013 and leaked thousands of classified documents exposing global surveillance — who is he?
Edward Snowden: Whistleblower and NSA contractor (born 1983)
One of the four basic animal tissue types, this thin protective cell layer lines blood vessels and body cavities and includes the skin's outer layer — what is it called?
Epithelium: Tissue lining the surfaces of organs in animals.
In this small bird of prey, females can be up to 25% larger than males — one of the biggest size gaps between sexes of any bird — and it hunts garden songbirds across Europe and Asia — which raptor?

Eurasian sparrowhawk: Species of bird. The Eurasian sparrowhawk (Accipiter nisus), also known as the northern sparrowhawk or simply the sparrowhawk, is a small bird of prey in the family Accipitridae.
Likely domesticated from the European polecat, with which it can still interbreed to produce hybrids, this slender mustelid averages about 50 centimeters long — what is it?
With atomic number 87 and a most stable isotope whose half-life is just 22 minutes, this alkali metal is the second-rarest naturally occurring element on Earth — which one?
Francium: Chemical element with atomic number 87 (Fr)

Published by Einstein in 1916 as a refinement of Newton's law of gravitation, this geometric framework describes gravity as curved spacetime, summed up by Wheeler as 'space-time tells matter how to move; matter tells space-time how to curve'?
General relativity: Theory of gravitation as curved spacetime. The relation is specified by the Einstein field equations, a system of second-order partial differential equations.
Dubbed the 'king of the birds' in European folklore for its golden head crest, this tiny kinglet's scientific name literally means 'petty king' — which bird?
Goldcrest: Small passerine bird in the kinglet family.
Caused by a hormone imbalance between estrogens and androgens, which benign condition results in enlarged breast tissue in men?
Gynecomastia: Enlargement of the human male breast.

This French mathematician, famous for his work in algebraic topology, came from an almost absurdly mathematical dynasty: son of mathematician Élie, nephew of mathematician Anna, and brother to a composer, a physicist, and yet another mathematician — who was he?
This small rodent, pointed-snouted with large rounded ears, has become the standard laboratory model organism after thriving alongside human settlements — what is it?
This physical phenomenon describes how a system's current state depends on its past history, forming looping curves in magnets and giving hard disk drives their memory — what is it?
Hysteresis: Dependence of the state of a system on its history. Hysteresis can be found in physics, chemistry, engineering, biology, and economics.
This condition restricts blood flow to tissue, starving cells of oxygen and nutrients due to causes like thrombosis or embolism — what's it called?
Ischemia: Restriction in blood supply to tissues.
This British chemical engineer founded a major chemicals group in 1998 and later became a minority shareholder with control over football operations at Manchester United — who is he?
Jim Ratcliffe: British engineer and businessman (born 1952)
Its subfamily name literally means 'large foot,' it's native to Australia and New Guinea, and a 2019 government tally counted some 42.8 million of them in harvest areas. Which marsupial?
Kangaroo: Marsupial of the family Macropodidae.
This is the most abundant genus of trees on Earth, dominating the boreal forests of Siberia and Canada despite dropping its needles every fall. What genus is it?
Larch: Genus of deciduous conifers in the family Pinaceae.
Also called May bells or Our Lady's tears, this woodland plant's sweetly scented white bell-flowers hide a dangerously poisonous secret — which flower?
Lily of the valley: Species of flowering plant in the asparagus family.
This best-known stag beetle species in Western Europe lends its genus its very name, and is currently listed as Near Threatened — what is it?
Lucanus cervus: Species of beetle. L. cervus is listed as Near Threatened by the IUCN Red List.

One of the most colorful mammals alive, this West African monkey sports vivid red-and-blue facial skin and lives in huge groups called 'hordes' — though long mistaken for a baboon, it's actually closer kin to mangabeys. What is it?
Mandrill: Species of Old World monkey from Africa.
Its name means 'big tooth,' and this extinct giant mackerel shark — once mistaken for a great white relative — is known only from fragmentary remains. What is it?
Megalodon: Extinct giant shark species. Megalodon probably had a major impact on the structure of marine communities.
This branch of economics studies how individual firms and consumers allocate scarce resources, as opposed to the economy-wide view of its counterpart — which field?
Microeconomics: Behavior of individuals and firms.

Étienne Geoffroy split these simians into 'Old World' Catarrhini and 'New World' Platyrrhini groups, and counting them without the apes leaves a famously incomplete family tree — what common-name animal is this?
Monkey: Animal of the "higher primates", excluding apes.
Native to southern Europe and North Africa, this fragrant evergreen shrub has berries that are macerated in alcohol to make Mirto liqueur — which plant?
Myrtus communis: Species of flowering plant.
Present in 26 African countries with one of its largest undisturbed populations at Kenya's Lake Turkana, which large crocodilian sees adult males reach 3.5 to 5 metres long?

Distinct from an unrelated American family with a similar name, these small seed-eating birds include house- and tree-dwelling species that nest on buildings in huge city numbers — which bird family is this?
Old World sparrow: Family of songbirds. Old World sparrows are groups of small passerine birds forming the family Passeridae.
Nicknamed 'forever chemicals' for their long environmental lifetimes, this class of synthetic compounds has been used in everything from Teflon to firefighting foam since 1938 — what's it called?
PFAS: Class of perfluorinated chemical compounds.
This hickory species native to the Mississippi River region produces a nut used in praline candy and a famous holiday pie, and is the official state tree of Texas — what is it?
Pecan: Species of nut tree native to the southern USA and northern Mexico.
The body produces about a quart of this substance daily to trap airborne particles and bacteria — coughed up, it's also known as sputum. What is it?
Phlegm: Mucus produced by the respiratory system (excluding the nasal passages)
Commonly called frangipani, this fragrant flowering shrub native to Mexico and the Caribbean is now a beloved ornamental in Hawaii and desert climates of Arabia — what genus is it?
Plumeria: Genus of flowering plants endemic to the Americas.
Defined as supervising a team to hit all its goals within three primary constraints — scope, time, and budget — what is this discipline?
Project management: Practice of leading the work of a team to achieve goals and criteria at a specified time.

Found across Africa, Asia, and Australia, this family of nonvenomous snakes — including some of the world's largest — must coil around prey and squeeze it into cardiac arrest before swallowing it whole. What is the family?
Pythonidae: Family of snakes. The taxonomy of pythons has evolved, and they are now known to be more closely related to sunbeam snakes and the Mexican burrowing python.
Spanning turtles, crocodilians, the lizards-and-snakes of Squamata, and the lone tuatara, which group of ectothermic, amniotic animals does herpetology study?
Reptile: Class of animals. The study of the traditional reptile orders, customarily in combination with the study of modern amphibians, is called herpetology.
With over three hundred species and tens of thousands of cultivars, this thorny, often-fragrant flowering shrub blooms in shades from white to pink, red, orange, and yellow — which plant?

First used in English in the early 15th century and possibly named after a Mediterranean island, this term covers small oily forage fish under 15 centimeters, with larger ones called pilchards — what's the fish?
Sardine: Common name for various small, oily forage fish.
